concerns.text: Task T012 (loss_functions.py) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly states 'Dependency: Requires T011 (recursive_llama.py) to be complete.' A task consuming an artifact from T011 cannot be parallel-safe relative to T011. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule and the definition of the [P] tag.

Task T013 (train.py) is marked [P] but lists 'Dependency: Requires T012 to be complete.' Since T012 is not parallel-safe (see above), T013 cannot be parallel-safe either. The [P] tag is incorrect and creates a false ordering implication.

Task T019 (run_benchmarks.py) depends on T004b (GSM8K/MMLU data). T004b is marked [P] but is a data-fetching task. While T004b can run in parallel with other setup tasks, T019 cannot start until T004b completes. The [P] tag on T019 is misleading if it implies independence from T004b's completion, though the dependency note is present. The primary issue is the lack of explicit ordering enforcement in the [P] tag logic for data consumers.

Phase 6 tasks (T042-T047) are marked [P] and grouped under 'Review-Driven Validation'. However, T042 depends on T012 (loss logic), T043/T044/T046 depend on T018 (metrics), and T045/T047 depend on T024/T025 (stats). These tasks are NOT parallel-safe relative to the foundational US2/US3 implementation tasks they extend. Marking them [P] suggests they can run before US2/US3 are complete, violating the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

Task T004b is marked [P] but is a data-fetching task that produces an artifact (gsm8k.json) consumed by T019 and T020. While T004b can run in parallel with T004a, the [P] tag should not imply it has no dependencies on the *completion* of the fetch for downstream tasks. The tag is technically correct for T004b itself (no upstream deps), but the downstream consumers (T019, T020) are incorrectly marked [P] in Phase 4, creating a semantic ordering conflict.
